nodes.label: Lead to Sales System — Architecture Document
nodes.rationale: Built via ADD (Attribute-Driven Design) in 9 incremental iterations, each closing goal→elements→concepts→instantiation→decisions→driver coverage. Contains context/container/component/deployment views, 27 sequence diagrams, port contracts, event catalog and Design Decision Records with discarded alternatives. Sized for ~10 agencies / ~9,000 leads/month, scalable x10 without structural redesign.

nodes.label: Coordinator Agent (LangGraph)
nodes.rationale: LangGraph orchestration with persistent checkpoints; new nodes (Qualification Iter.3, Recommendation Iter.4, Appointment Iter.5) added without touching existing nodes (QA-06). Stateless workers with retry/backoff — conversation state lives in Postgres, not process memory, enabling 24/7 availability and horizontal scaling without session affinity.

nodes.label: Conversation State Machine (persisted FSM)
nodes.rationale: Explicit FSM persisted in Postgres with Dormant/Reactivated/OwnershipEvaluation as first-class states — makes QA-09 verifiable by construction: invalid transition raises InvalidTransitionError with no write. Survives restarts (dormancy spans months). Discarded: ad-hoc boolean flags, in-memory FSM.

nodes.label: Guardrail Interceptor
nodes.rationale: Maximum-priority layer executed BEFORE Coordinator reasoning, with direct bypass to the Ownership Policy Engine — zero latency and determinism for '¿Está María?' (scenario 8). Discarded: letting the LLM decide the bypass (non-deterministic, unacceptable for a hard rule). Since Iteration 7 reads its rules from the Guardrail Configuration Service instead of hardcoded Rules 1-4.

nodes.label: Ownership Policy Engine (Decision Table)
nodes.rationale: Grew skeleton (scenarios 1+8, Iter.2) → +scenario 2 (Iter.5) → full 10-scenario Decision Table with PolicyRules ordered by priority (Iter.6), never changing the evaluate(context)->OwnershipDecision signature — QA-06 validated four consecutive times. Unimplemented scenarios returned explicit NotImplementedPlaceholder, never silent defaults. Property-based tests guarantee exactly one rule wins per evaluation. Discarded: if/elif chains, Drools-style full rule engine (over-engineering).

nodes.label: Chatwoot Webhook Adapter (ACL)
nodes.rationale: Anti-Corruption Layer translating Chatwoot events to domain events and back; acks webhooks in <1s while the Coordinator processes asynchronously via the Event Bus (QA-01) — decouples LLM latency from webhook timeout. Future channels (Telegram, QA-04) only touch this adapter.

nodes.label: AI Sidebar Publisher
nodes.rationale: Publishes state, ownership and explanations into Chatwoot for broker consumption — explainability by construction: explanation fields are first-class, not derived logs (QA-11).

nodes.label: Event Bus (Transactional Outbox/Inbox)
nodes.rationale: Outbox+Inbox over the same Postgres: event written in the same transaction as the domain change (no inconsistency window), single-writer worker publishes, consumers deduplicate by event_id (at-least-once, idempotent handlers). Discarded: Kafka/RabbitMQ day 1 (operational overhead unjustified at ~0.07 events/sec), naive dual-write.

nodes.label: Versioned Configuration Store
nodes.rationale: One versioned-table-with-active-flag pattern reused three consecutive times: OrganizationConfig, PromptTemplate/PromptVersion, and OwnershipPolicy — versioning and rollback for free, single point of config resolution avoiding per-module settings sprawl (CRN-9). transcriptSource field reserved from Iteration 1 to avoid a later schema migration.

nodes.label: Row-Level Security by organization_id
nodes.rationale: Entry middleware resolves organizationId and executes SET app.current_org before any module query — isolation enforced by the database engine as defense in depth, impossible to 'forget' the filter. Discarded: schema-per-tenant and database-per-tenant (Phase 4 architecture, violates single-deployment constraint).

nodes.label: Lead Sync Adapter (bidirectional ACL)
nodes.rationale: Sole read/write point to wacrm (RBAC + audit centralized, QA-08). CDC via polling with syncedAt watermark cursor — resumable after any crash, works even if wacrm webhooks are unreliable. Writes to wacrm go through the same Outbox pattern.

nodes.label: Staleness Guard
nodes.rationale: Explicitly invoked before every critical decision; forces synchronous re-sync if isStale() exceeds 60s, blocking the decision until data is fresh — materializes QA-13 as verifiable behavior, not documentation. Discarded: trusting periodic polling alone (a crashed worker breaks QA-13 silently).

nodes.label: Completeness Gate (Specification pattern)
nodes.rationale: External precondition of the Qualification→Recommendation transition (QA-14): completeness < threshold returns false + missing dimension, prompting a targeted question. Kept outside the FSM so the FSM stays generic and the business rule has a single point of truth.

nodes.label: BuyerProfile Capture Service (progressive profiling)
nodes.rationale: Captures the buyer profile one dimension at a time as a LangGraph node (Prompt Chaining) — each sub-question is simple and verifiable, reducing compounded error. Discarded: single capture form (worse conversational UX, higher abandonment).

nodes.label: Hybrid Retrieval (SQL filters + pgvector)
nodes.rationale: Structured SQL filters (budget/zone/type) discard impossible candidates cheaply, then pgvector semantic search over the filtered subset captures qualitative intent — better precision than either alone. Discarded: pure RAG (could return properties over budget), pure SQL (misses unstructured intent). Embeddings precalculated at ingestion, never generated per search.

nodes.label: Ranking Engine (deterministic, no LLM)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic score = Σ(RankingSignal.weight × value); adding a new signal never changes the signature (QA-10). Discarded: LLM ranking over the property list (non-deterministic, breaks auditability and explainability).

nodes.label: Explanation Generator
nodes.rationale: Receives only the winning RankingSignals; the LLM only phrases them into natural language, never decides content — every explanation is traceable to a real signal, preventing hallucinated reasons (QA-11). The LLM never sees the full property list.

nodes.label: Neighborhood Enrichment Adapter
nodes.rationale: Fan-out/fan-in parallel Google Maps calls over only the final Top-3 (not all candidates — bounds cost/latency); on timeout delivers a partial fallback and completes asynchronously via NeighborhoodEnriched event — latency budget (<15s) prioritized over message completeness.

nodes.label: Availability Validator (deterministic bottleneck)
nodes.rationale: Mandatory validation bottleneck before proposing or confirming any slot, with owner/admin confirmation when no real-time inventory state exists and automatic re-validation 2-4h before the visit. Deterministic and auditable — does not depend on the LLM 'remembering' to check. Never caches beyond a short TTL.

nodes.label: Scheduling Service
nodes.rationale: Materializes a validated visit as an Appointment; requires AvailabilityValidatorPort status=confirmed; internally invokes the Calendar Adapter with conferenceData.createRequest.

nodes.label: Google Calendar Adapter
nodes.rationale: Single port: create_event with conferenceData.createRequest returns event + Meet hangoutLink in one API call — no separate Meet port or adapter exists, reflecting the real mechanism. Discarded: modeling Meet as an independent integration (duplicated architecture over a single call).

nodes.label: Reminder Scheduler
nodes.rationale: 24h/2h reminders persisted as jobs in Postgres, independent of the synchronous booking flow — survives restarts of the process that booked. Same scheduling pattern as decayToDormant() and Follow-up Scheduler.

nodes.label: Handoff Package Builder (Facade)
nodes.rationale: Assembles profile + recommendations + conversation summary exclusively through existing ports (BuyerProfileCapturePort, RecommendationPort, FSM) — never direct table access across modules. The broker never receives a 'blank' conversation.

nodes.label: Outcome Listener
nodes.rationale: Listens to DealClosed/VisitCompleted/ClosedLost and links the real business result — known weeks later — to the original OwnershipDecision, accumulating the Phase 3 ML training signal without future schema change. The Coordinator cannot write the outcome at decision time because it doesn't exist yet.

nodes.label: Reactivation Detector
nodes.rationale: The ONLY component authorized to emit ReactivationEvent; verifies the conversation is Dormant before emitting. Follow-up Scheduler and Campaign Dispatcher never invoke the Ownership Policy Engine directly — no signal generator decides the owner.

nodes.label: ReactivationEvent (domain event)
nodes.rationale: Sole trigger of OwnershipEvaluation; payload includes source (reply | campaign | new_property). Ensures no reactivation path bypasses policy evaluation (QA-09).

nodes.label: Follow-up Scheduler
nodes.rationale: Independent job triggered by Dormant transitions per org-configured thresholds; fires nurturing messages but never assigns an owner.

nodes.label: Campaign Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: Batch campaigns to cold leads with per-lead response tracking; never invokes the Ownership Policy Engine directly — replies flow through the Reactivation Detector.

nodes.label: Admin Gateway (versioned CRUD + RBAC)
nodes.rationale: Thin layer over existing Configuration Store ports; versioned CRUD with rollback for prompts, org config and ownership policies. RBAC with 4 roles per organization (owner, admin, broker, viewer), backed by RLS — roles never cross organization_id. Discarded: parallel admin data store, fine-grained per-resource ACLs (over-engineering for a small team).

nodes.label: Tool Registry (passive catalog)
nodes.rationale: Catalogs each ToolDefinition (typed input/output schemas + riskLevel feeding guardrails); validates schemas once at registration, not per invocation — no latency added to the critical path.

nodes.label: Guardrail Configuration Service
nodes.rationale: Turns the journey's 4 hardcoded guardrail rules into per-organization data in the Configuration Store — rule adjustments no longer require a deploy. First documented modification of a prior iteration's component behavior.

nodes.label: Dashboard Query Service (CQRS read)
nodes.rationale: Read-only aggregation over AIDecisionTrace with materialized views (cost per agent, p95 latency, decisions/hour) — trace reads never compete with the critical business write path. Segmentation Dashboard (Iter.8) extends it rather than creating a separate service.

nodes.label: Meet Transcript Adapter (Strategy)
nodes.rationale: Strategy over transcriptSource (agency_workspace | platform_default), reusing the field reserved in OrganizationConfig since Iteration 1 — closes the transcripts driver without schema migration; encapsulates the data-governance difference between agency and platform perimeters; never mixes both modes for one organization.

nodes.label: Conversation Mining Pipeline (batch ETL)
nodes.rationale: Asynchronous batch ETL over the accumulated MessageRef archive + transcripts, outside the conversational critical path; can reprocess the full corpus without affecting production. Real-time per-conversation extraction discarded — insights are aggregates.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph Builder (incremental)
nodes.rationale: Consumes existing domain events (MessageReceived/VisitCompleted/DealClosed) to update the graph incrementally instead of full rebuilds that grow costlier as the corpus grows; persists nodes/relations in Postgres+pgvector.

nodes.label: Market Insight Discovery Service
nodes.rationale: Derives Buyer Personas, ICPs and trends from the Knowledge Graph with MANDATORY provenance — no insight is applied automatically to a prompt or ranking signal without a verifiable source and admin approval via the Admin Gateway. Same explainability principle as OwnershipDecision and RecommendationItem.

nodes.label: AIDecisionTrace (aggregate)
nodes.rationale: One record per AI decision: agent, prompt version, tool calls, context refs, cost, latency, output (QA-07 / ARSDA Gate 9). OpenTelemetry instrumented from the FIRST request with generic fields, avoiding costly observability retrofitting; agentName/promptVersionId populate once real agents exist.

nodes.label: OwnershipDecision (auditable record)
nodes.rationale: Persistent record of each policy evaluation: input snapshot, selected owner, human-readable explanation (QA-11) — auditable and replayable. Paired with OwnershipOutcome it becomes the Phase 3 ML training dataset, captured from Sprint 4 with no schema change required.
